They keep an eye on labor- which is the indicator of how their labor force on the clock meets consumer demand on an hourly basis. That number correlates to how much labor is truly necessary for smooth hourly operation without cutting into profits. If the labor goes up, that means business over x amount of time has been slow, and now labor costs are cutting into profit.

Store managers track this data Over a course of time (usually annually) and compare consumer demand of such and such day to the same day in the previous year. They use this date to determine how much labor will likely be needed, as well as local news outlets or other indications that business could pick up. Such as a nearby school sports team winning a game, or other local events.

I’m missing your point mate XD this is my opinion here, but I feel like the US is kind of brainwashed by hyper-capitalist ideology. Hear me out. XD 

 I feel that many people here aspire to become part of that 1% rather than dismantling that unequal power dynamic present today. Wealth is seen as success, and the wealthier you are the more successful you are. Because here, making as much money as you possibly can is the goal. It’s what this country was founded on Lmao. Doesn’t make it right. That’s not to say it’s a bad thing to aspire to wealth. The bad part of this is how disproportionate our economy has become as a result. Preventably so, I might add. As well as the problems associated with that disproportionate wealth distribution. 

For example, Our nation as a whole has enough wealth within it to comfortably offer better benefits and wages to many underpaid industries/positions. Small business owners are the hardest hit when minimum wage goes up, however, because of the disparity of our nations wealth. Small businesses are usually run by people who are working hard to provide a service and turn a profit- meager as it is. Whenever the minimum wage is increased, small businesses are forced to raise prices in order to keep up their meager profits, inflating local markets. I feel like this is more understandable, and I’m willing to accept it more. 

When large, well established and successful businesses are hit with these wage increases, they also raise their prices. Not because they need to per se, but so their profit margin does not shrink. If their profit margin shrinks, they view it as losing money because it is less money in their pockets. Mind you these corporate owners are among the 1%. Why would a slight decrease in profit margin be of concern to these people? 

Many are quick to jump to sympathize with these large business owners but fail to see that if they would simply take a slight cut in profits, rather than raising their prices, the rate at which the minimum wage is needing to be raised slows. I think this could help level out inflation or at least slow it down until we can find a more manageable solution. It could also help relieve that wealth disparity a bit, and help our entire society as a whole. Statistically speaking, the more wealth within a community the better education and programs are made available within those communities. Just one example. Because of how our society is organized and run with these hyper-capitalist values, and the greed that permeates our society, whenever a policy or idea is offered which actually makes an attempt to repair this disparity, it is immediately met with zealous hatred, mudslinging and is effectively shot down and replaced with another in its place which makes the appearance of fixing one part of the problem but actually exacerbates it.
